title: Remarks at Louisiana, Missouri
paragraphs: Mr. Congressman; Mr. Mayor, and you, My Fellow Citizens:

It is indeed a great pleasure to be in historic Pike County. I have heard a great deal of pike county. I know its fertility; I know its good roads; I know the extraordinary nursery you have got right here, a nursery of a double kind by the way; I passed the new dynamite factory. I congratulate you on all your products but I want to say that what counts finally as the best type of product is the men and women, and therefore, as I like your stock, I want to congratulate you on the children. And one word to them, and it applies just as much to those of an older growth, I believe in play and I believe in work. When you play, play hard, and when you work do not play at all. I have enjoyed greatly coming here into your great and beautiful state. I congratulate you upon the prosperity which we are all enjoying. There will come ups and downs in that prosperity, but on the whole as sure as there is a sun in Heaven, the tendency will be upward when you have a race like ours standing on a continent as a base. We are sometimes criticised for a vein of boastfulness in talking of the future of our country. Men and women, we cannot overestimate what that future will be if we are only true to ourselves. We must have, as a base of that future as a foundation, material prosperity, material well-being, but that is only the base, only the foundation. Upon it must be built as a superstructure the quality for the lack of which no material well-being can atone, the qualities of devotion to an ideal, of lofty adherence to the right for the right's sake, of rugged power to achieve that ideal in practical methods. It is a fine thing to have a strong body, it is a better thing to have a strong mind, and best of a, ll is it to have that which counts for more than body, for more than mind -- character. In character I include not only the passive virtues, not only the abstention from wrong, but the power to war effectively for the right. I include the qualities which made our people alike those that wore the blue and those who wore the gray leave an imperishable heritage of renown for their children and their children's children in the times that tried men's souls. (Applause.)

I am on my way to St. Louis to commemorate the time a century ago when this great country became a part of the United States. I thank you for coming here, I appreciate it to the full, and I wish you for the future an even greater share of the well-being which you now so abundantly enjoy. (Cheers and applause)
